mechanisms.text: Inserted documents are chunked, entities and relations extracted, and persisted to a working directory; the graph and all contexts are reloaded from that directory on next initialization
Local query mode retrieves top-K community reports and entity context into prompt; global mode uses top-K important and central communities up to a configurable cap
Entity extraction converts raw text into structured knowledge by identifying entities and relationships, then stores results in both graph and vector databases.
Three distinct storage backend abstractions are defined: key-value storage, vector storage, and graph storage, each scoped to a named namespace.
Documents are split into overlapping token-sized chunks, each keyed by an MD5 hash of content with a 'chunk-' prefix, and stored in a KV store.
Retrieve-only mode available: query can return only the retrieved context rather than a generated answer, for integration into custom prompts
working_dir is per-instantiation (defaults to timestamped directory), providing implicit session-level isolation of all storage namespaces.
LLM calls support a hashing KV cache, allowing repeated LLM prompts to be served from storage rather than re-called
Entity names and descriptions are upserted into a vector store (entity_vdb) to enable similarity-based retrieval.
Global search uses only top-K communities by importance rather than filling all communities into context
Local retrieval enforces separate token ceilings for text units, local context, and community reports.
Incremental insertion with MD5-hash-based deduplication for content-based duplicate detection
nano-graphrag indexes a corpus; indexing time is reported as a benchmark metric.
LLM response caching is supported via a hashing KV storage passed through kwargs
nano-graphrag supports NetworkX (in-memory) and Neo4j as graph storage backends
LLM function signature supports a hashing KV cache for memoizing LLM calls

ledger.claim: Text chunks are persisted as keyed records in a KV store, identified by MD5 hash of content with 'chunk-' prefix.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Entity extraction uses iterative LLM gleaning: the model is re-prompted to continue extracting until it signals completion or a max iteration count is reached.
ledger.quote:
for now_glean_index in range(entity_extract_max_gleaning):
            glean_result = await use_llm_func(continue_prompt, history_messages=history)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Node merge conflict resolution: entity type is chosen by majority vote across all extracted instances; descriptions are deduplicated, concatenated, then LLM-summarized if over token limit.
ledger.quote:
entity_type = sorted(
        Counter(
            [dp["entity_type"] for dp in nodes_data] + already_entitiy_types
        ).items(),
        key=lambda x: x[1],
        reverse=True,
    )[0][0]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Edge merge conflict resolution: weights are summed, descriptions deduplicated and joined, source IDs unioned, and the result upserted.
ledger.quote:
weight = sum([dp["weight"] for dp in edges_data] + already_weights)
    description = GRAPH_FIELD_SEP.join(
        sorted(set([dp["description"] for dp in edges_data] + already_description))
    )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Entity descriptions and names are stored in a vector store for similarity-based retrieval at query time.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Community reports are persisted to a KV store after hierarchical generation, level-by-level from deepest to shallowest.
ledger.quote:
levels = sorted(set([c["level"] for c in community_values]), reverse=True)
    logger.info(f"Generating by levels: {levels}")
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: At query time, community reports are filtered by level and minimum rating before retrieval, making retrieval policy conditional rather than always-retrieve.
ledger.quote:
community_datas = [
        c
        for c in community_datas
        if c["report_json"].get("rating", 0) >= query_param.global_min_community_rating
    ]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: No session or user isolation is implemented in this file; all storage instances are passed in as shared parameters with no per-user or per-session scoping visible here.
ledger.quote:
async def extract_entities(
    chunks: dict[str, TextChunkSchema],
    knwoledge_graph_inst: BaseGraphStorage,
    entity_vdb: BaseVectorStorage,
    tokenizer_wrapper,
    global_config: dict,
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store contains curated graph facts (entity nodes, relationship edges, community reports), not a raw message log or full conversation transcript.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Three storage abstractions (KV, vector, graph) are namespaced, enabling per-namespace isolation of persisted data.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Upsert (not append) is the write primitive for all three stores, meaning re-ingesting the same id overwrites rather than duplicates.
ledger.quote:
async def upsert(self, data: dict[str, T]):
        raise NotImplementedError
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Community reports attach to graph communities and are a persisted field (report_string, report_json) beyond the raw schema.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval into context is token-budget-gated per content type (text units, local context, community reports), not a flat top-k.
ledger.quote:
local_max_token_for_text_unit: int = 4000  # 12000 * 0.33
    local_max_token_for_local_context: int = 4800  # 12000 * 0.4
    local_max_token_for_community_report: int = 3200  # 12000 * 0.27
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The write path persists curated facts (named entities and typed relationships with descriptions) into a graph store and a vector store — not a raw message log.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Documents are deduplicated at insert time via content hash; already-stored docs are silently skipped.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: There is no conversation-level message log; the store contains document chunks, entity graphs, and community reports — not a dialogue transcript.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Storage isolation is at the working_dir level; no per-user or per-character isolation mechanism is present in this file.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Working directory persists all graph contexts and is reloaded automatically on re-initialization
ledger.quote: Next time you initialize a GraphRAG from the same working_dir, it will reload all the contexts automatically.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Community structure in the stored graph is fully recomputed on every insert, not incrementally updated
ledger.quote: each time you insert, the communities of graph will be re-computed and the community reports will be re-generated
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Storage layer is fully swappable: KV, vector, and graph backends can each be replaced with custom implementations
ledger.quote: You can replace all storage-related components to your own implementation, nano-graphrag mainly uses three kinds of storage
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: LLM responses can be cached in a KV store keyed by hashed prompt to avoid redundant calls
ledger.quote: hashing_kv: BaseKVStorage = kwargs.pop("hashing_kv", None)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The covariates feature from the original GraphRAG is not implemented
ledger.quote: nano-graphrag didn't implement the covariates feature of GraphRAG
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag builds a graph store by extracting entities and relations via LLM; an empty extraction result leaves the graph empty and causes community detection to fail.
ledger.quote: This error is caused by nano-graphrag tries to compute communities on an empty network. In most cases, this is caused by the LLM model you're using, it fails to extract any entities or relations, so the graph is empty.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Entity extraction processes text in chunks; the log line 'Processed 42 chunks, 0 entities(duplicated), 0 relations(duplicated)' confirms chunk-level processing before graph storage.
ledger.quote: One possible reason of 'Processed 42 chunks,0 entities(duplicated),0 relations(duplicated)WARNING:nano-graphrag:Didn't extract any entities, maybe your LLM is not working WARNING:nano-graphrag:No new entities found'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag completes corpus indexing in under 4 minutes, faster than GraphRAG's 5+ minutes.
ledger.quote: nano-graphrag index time : less than 4 minutes

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag uses OpenAI Embedding and gpt-4o for both indexing and search.
ledger.quote: Both GraphRAG and nano-graphrag use OpenAI Embedding and gpt-4o .

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag's GraphRAG class accepts a configurable graph storage backend; Neo4jStorage is one such backend requiring Neo4j 5.x with the GDS plugin
ledger.quote:
from nano_graphrag._storage import Neo4jStorage
...GraphRAG(
    graph_storage_cls=Neo4jStorage,
    addon_params=neo4j_config,
)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Persisted state reloads automatically when GraphRAG is re-initialized from the same working directory
ledger.quote: Next time you initialize a GraphRAG from the same working_dir, it will reload all the contexts automatically.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph community index is fully recomputed on every insert, meaning the stored community reports are not incrementally updated but regenerated
ledger.quote: However, each time you insert, the communities of graph will be re-computed and the community reports will be re-generated
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All three storage layers (KV, vector, graph) are replaceable via constructor arguments, making persistence backend pluggable
ledger.quote: You can replace all storage-related components to your own implementation, nano-graphrag mainly uses three kinds of storage
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve-then-prompt path is explicitly exposed: only_need_context=True returns raw retrieved context without generation
ledger.quote: you can use param=QueryParam(..., only_need_context=True,...), which will only return the retrieved context from graph
ledger.locator: readme.md, Only query the related context section
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Global search retrieve policy limits candidates to top-K communities by importance/centrality, not full community set
ledger.quote: nano-graphrag only use the top-K important and central communites (use QueryParam.global_max_consider_community to control, default to 512 communities).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: LLM calls support a hashing KV cache layer to avoid redundant LLM requests
ledger.quote:
# pop cache KV database if any
hashing_kv: BaseKVStorage = kwargs.pop("hashing_kv", None)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph backend configuration is supplied via global_config["addon_params"]
ledger.quote: Config would follow the existing pattern via `global_config["addon_params"]` with `arcadedb_url` and `arcadedb_auth` keys.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag supports an in-memory graph backend (NetworkX) as one storage option
ledger.quote: nano-graphrag currently supports NetworkX (in-memory) and Neo4j as graph backends.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.label: inferred

ledger.quote: No cryptographic protections mentioned for local storage (NetworkX, nano-vectordb) or inter-component communication.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Deduplication is content-based (MD5 hash), not semantic
ledger.quote: Incremental insertion uses MD5-hash for deduplication; duplicate detection is content-based, not semantic.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: No multi-user or multi-tenant architecture; isolation is per working directory only
ledger.quote: The architecture is single-user, working from a local working_dir. Multi-tenancy would require custom application-layer separation.

ledger.claim: nano-graphrag persists extracted entities and relationships into both graph and vector databases after chunking and LLM-based extraction.
ledger.quote: Storage: The structured data populates both graph and vector databases
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Retrieval at query time uses vector similarity as the entry point for both naive and local modes; local mode additionally traverses the knowledge graph.
ledger.quote: First, it identifies entities in the query using vector similarity search. It then explores the neighborhood of these entities in the knowledge graph
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Global search selects from stored community reports, filtered and sorted, rather than raw entity lookup.
ledger.quote: It retrieves community schemas from the knowledge graph. Communities are sorted by occurrence and filtered by level. The system extracts the most relevant points from community reports
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Importance score on entities (0–1) is part of the stored data model, implying weight-based retrieval selection is possible.
ledger.quote: importance_score: A value (0-1) indicating significance
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: State persisted to working_dir is reloaded automatically on next initialization
ledger.quote: Next time you initialize a GraphRAG from the same working_dir, it will reload all the contexts automatically.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Communities and community reports are regenerated on every insert, not incrementally updated
ledger.quote: each time you insert, the communities of graph will be re-computed and the community reports will be re-generated
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Global search retrieves only top-K central communities, not the full community set as in original GraphRAG
ledger.quote: nano-graphrag only use the top-K important and central communites (use QueryParam.global_max_consider_community to control, default to 512 communities)
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Default KV storage backend is disk file; default vector storage is nano-vectordb; default graph storage is networkx
ledger.quote: By default we use disk file storage as the backend ... By default we use nano-vectordb as the backend ... By default we use networkx as the backend.
